comment: Section 3.6.5 addresses conformance testing before and during procurement. It does not address behavioral drift in AI-enabled DPI-H components after deployment — the condition where an AI component that achieved conformance at procurement behaves differently after updates, changes to upstream data sources, or integration with new system components, without triggering re-conformance testing. For AI components used in clinical decision support or population health analytics, behavioral drift may represent a patient safety issue that the current conformance framework would not detect.

public.text: Section 3.6.5 addresses conformance testing before and during procurement. It does not address behavioral drift in AI-enabled DPI-H components after deployment — the condition where an AI component that achieved conformance at procurement behaves differently after updates, changes to upstream data sources, or integration with new system components, without triggering re-conformance testing. For AI components used in clinical decision support or population health analytics, behavioral drift may represent a patient safety issue that the current conformance framework would not detect.
public.suggestedRevision: Add after line 961: "For AI-enabled DPI-H components, conformance testing should extend beyond point-in-time procurement validation to include: (a) defined thresholds at which behavioral drift from the conformance baseline requires re-testing; (b) post-deployment monitoring protocols that compare AI component behavior against its conformance baseline at defined intervals; and (c) a documented process for detecting and responding to retrospective evaluation integrity failures — cases where a conformance evaluation is later found to have been conducted in a misconfigured or unrepresentative environment. These requirements align with the NIST AI RMF MANAGE function (MANAGE 2.4), which addresses ongoing monitoring and retrospective evaluation integrity protocols."
